title: How to Choose the Right Optical Filter for Fluorescence Imaging, Point Detection, and Raman Spectroscopy
summary: Compare optical filters for fluorescence imaging, Raman spectroscopy, and point detection systems.

Optical filters shape performance in fluorescence imaging, flow cytometry, Raman spectroscopy and biomedical analytical systems. Filter selection directly impacts how much signal light reaches the detector, how effectively unwanted light is suppressed, and how cleanly spectral channels are separated from each other.


However, not all optical systems require the same level of filter performance. At IDEX Health & Science, our[Semrock optical filters](https://www.idex-hs.com/capabilities/semrock-optical-filters) are intentionally engineered across well-defined performance tiers based upon your application needs. This tiered approach enables selecting filters that meet application requirements without adding unnecessary cost or complexity. Whether you need essential performance, maximum signal, or maximum contrast, selecting the right performance level ensures your system performs as intended.


## Introduction to Semrock Filter Performance Tiers


Across all Semrock filter families, performance is driven by three core spectral criteria:


- **Transmission**
- **Blocking depth and wavelength coverage**
- **Edge steepness**
- **Transition width**


> **Performance tradeoffs result in two primary product tiers:**
>
>
> -[Essential Performance](https://www.idex-hs.com/docs/default-source/catalogs/smk-essential-performance-catalog.pdf?sfvrsn=983394d7_7) filters prioritize reliable, application‑matched performance with relaxed specifications that reduce cost.
> -[High Performance](https://www.idex-hs.com/docs/default-source/catalogs/semrock-high-performance-optical-filter-catalog.pdf?sfvrsn=c01b8106_3) filters are engineered to maximize brightness or contrast, delivering higher signal‑to‑noise ratios for demanding imaging and detection tasks.

## Essential Performance Optical Filters


Essential Performance optical filters are designed for applications that do not require the most demanding spectral specifications but still need consistent, reliable optical behavior.


This tier is well‑suited for:


- Standard fluorescence imaging where the price point is prioritized
- Raman applications with moderate spectral requirements
- Detection systems using point detectors
- Cost‑sensitive OEM devices and research instruments


By selectively relaxing specifications that are not critical to system performance, Essential Performance filters balance performance without compromising Semrock quality or reliability.


###
Essential Performance Filter Families


#### BrightLine Basic Sets


[BrightLine Basic sets](https://www.idex-hs.com/store/products/semrock_optical_filters/optical_filter_sets/1?semrock_filter_families=BrightLine+Basic%E2%84%A2+Fluorescence+Filters) are engineered specifically for fluorescence imaging applications that benefit from standardized specifications and simplified selection. These sets have relaxed spectral requirements to meet common fluorophore needs at a lower cost while remaining versatile and budget-friendly with Semrock quality. **BrightLine Basic is the only imaging set offered within the Essential Performance tier.**


#### EdgeBasic Filters


[EdgeBasic long‑wave pass and short‑wave pass filters](https://www.idex-hs.com/store/products/semrock_optical_filters/individual_optical_filters/1?semrock_filter_families=EdgeBasic%E2%84%A2+Filters) are optimized for Raman spectroscopy and selected fluorescence applications. They provide deep laser‑line blocking and high transmission, but their relaxed transition widths will not allow measurement of the narrowest Raman shifts or ultra‑steep spectral transitions.


#### Nanopede Filters


[Nanopede bandpass filters](https://www.idex-hs.com/store/products/semrock_optical_filters/individual_optical_filters/1?semrock_filter_families=Nanopede%E2%84%A2+Filters) are designed for **non‑imaging, point-based** detection applications, such as spectral flow cytometry. They offer discrete, evenly spaced spectral coverage across UV, visible, and near‑infrared spectral regions, supporting flexible detection configurations.


###
Essential Performance Benefits


Across Essential Performance families, filters are designed to deliver:


- Balanced transmission, blocking, and edge steepness
- Tailored performance solutions aligned to application needs
- Dependable optical performance for both imaging (BrightLine Basic) and point detection systems (EdgeBasic and Nanopede)


## High Performance Optical Filters


High Performance optical filters are engineered for applications where signal quality and / or signal-to-noise ratio is paramount. These filters are optimized for modern imaging systems that require high brightness, high contrast, and precise spectral separation when multiplexing.


This tier addresses challenges such as:


- Closely spaced excitation and emission spectra
- High detector sensitivity over a broad wavelength range
- Fluorophores with short Stokes shifts
- Modern LED- and laser‑based illumination systems


High Performance families provide increased transmission, deeper and broader blocking, and steeper spectral edges, delivering darker backgrounds and thus higher signal‑to‑noise ratios.


### High Performance Filter Families


#### BrightLine Filter Sets


The BrightLine family established Semrock hard‑coated filter technology in life science applications. Known for durability, spectral reliability, and repeatable edge placement,[BrightLine sets](https://www.idex-hs.com/store/products/semrock_optical_filters/optical_filter_sets/1?semrock_filter_families=BrightLine%C2%AE+Fluorescence+Filters) remain a proven solution for general fluorescence imaging.


**BrightLine is the only filter family offering multi-band sets for multiplexing applications, including full multi-band, Pinkel, and Sedat sets.**


#### BrightLine 2.0 Filter Sets


[BrightLine 2.0](https://www.idex-hs.com/store/products/semrock_optical_filters/optical_filter_sets/1?semrock_filter_families=BrightLine%C2%AE+2.0+Fluorescence+Filters) builds on the BrightLine legacy with enhanced specifications tailored for modern imaging workflows. These sets combine improved blocking and higher transmission with broader compatibility across current and legacy light sources and detectors, offering a strong balance of performance and versatility.


#### Avant Filter Sets


[Avant filters](https://www.idex-hs.com/store/products/semrock_optical_filters/optical_filter_sets/1?semrock_filter_families=Avant%E2%84%A2+Filters) represent Semrock’s highest level of spectral edge engineering. Designed to minimize the gap between excitation and emission passbands, Avant sets enable higher brightness (signal) for fluorophores with short Stokes shifts. Ultra‑steep edges at precisely placed wavelengths allow excitation closer to absorption peaks while collecting more emission light without sacrificing contrast.


#### RazorEdge Edge Filters and Dichroic Beamsplitters


Semrock stocks an unsurpassed selection of the highest performance[edge filters available for Raman Spectroscopy](https://www.idex-hs.com/store/products/semrock_optical_filters/individual_optical_filters/1?semrock_filter_families=RazorEdge%C2%AE+Raman+Filters&viewAll=true) , with edge wavelengths from 224 to 1319 nm. Now you can see the weakest signals closer to the laser line than you ever have before with optical filter technology. With their deep laser-line blocking, ultra-wide and low-ripple passbands, proven hard-coating reliability, and high laser damage threshold, they offer performance that lasts. Short-wave-pass edge filters are also available for Anti-Stokes Raman applications.


The unique RazorEdge Dichroic beamsplitters exhibit unparalleled performance, reflecting a standard laser line incident at 45° while efficiently passing the Raman-shifted wavelengths. They exhibit ultrasteep transition from reflection to transmission, far superior to filters available elsewhere. The guaranteed transition width of < 1% of the laser wavelength for U-grade and < 0.5% of the laser wavelength for E-grade (regardless of polarization) makes these filters a perfect match to our popular normal-incidence RazorEdge ultrasteep long-wave-pass filters.


#### MaxLine Laser-Line Filters


[Semrock MaxLine Laser-Line Filters](https://www.idex-hs.com/store/products/semrock_optical_filters/individual_optical_filters/1?semrock_filter_families=MaxLine%C2%AE+Laser-line+Clean-up+Filters) guarantee > 90% transmission at the laser line, while maintaining a narrow full-width, half-maximum (FWHM) by rapidly rolling off to an optical density of > 5 at wavelengths differing by only 1% from the laser wavelength, with OD > 6 at wavelength differing by only 1.5% from the laser wavelength. These steep edges create the perfect match to RazorEdge U-grade filters. For E-grade RazorEdge filters, new and steeper MaxLine E-grade filters increase the edge steepness, resulting in the perfect pairing for Raman signal collection even closer to the laser line.


The MaxLine filter spectrally “cleans up” the laser, allowing only the desired laser light to reach the sample. The RazorEdge U- or E-grade filter then removes the laser line from the light scattered off the sample while efficiently transmitting desired light at wavelengths close to the laser line.


#### Verona


Semrock’s long-pass[Verona optical filters](https://www.idex-hs.com/store/products/semrock_optical_filters/individual_optical_filters/1?semrock_filter_families=Verona%E2%84%A2+Filters&viewAll=true) provide industry-best solutions for deep blocking close to the laser line for Raman applications. The transition width of no more than 0.2% relative to the edge wavelength still achieves blocking > OD6 at the laser line. Our understanding of how crucial constant transmission is for the best collection of weak Raman signals is why we offer a filter with both low ripple and improved steepness from our RazorEdge™ series, making the Verona family the new gold standard for filter-based Raman analysis. Push the limits of what you can see with your Raman system with Verona Raman filters.


### High Performance Benefits


High Performance filter families are designed to:


- Increase Raman signal collection
- Improve signal‑to‑noise ratio (contrast) through deeper blocking
- Enable enhanced performance for short Stokes shift fluorophores via steeper edges
- Support modern detectors and illumination sources


## How to Choose the Right Optical Filter for Your Needs


**Choose Essential Performance if you:**


- Are performing routine imaging or detection, or
- Need to control system cost without sacrificing reliability


**Choose High Performance if you:**


- Require maximum brightness or contrast
- Use modern LEDs, lasers, or high‑sensitivity cameras
- Work with challenging fluorophores or tightly spaced multiplexing

#### FAQs


1. **What is the difference between BrightLine and BrightLine 2.0 filters?** Both[BrightLine and BrightLine 2.0 filter sets](https://www.idex-hs.com/news-events/stories-and-features/detail/enhanced-fluorescence-imaging-brightline-filter-sets) are designed for fluorescence imaging, but they are optimized for different imaging environments. BrightLine filters are a proven standard for fluorescence microscopy and remain an effective choice for many imaging systems. BrightLine 2.0 filters build on that foundation with enhanced transmission, deeper blocking, and improved spectral efficiency to maximize performance with modern LED and laser illumination sources while maintaining compatibility with legacy systems. These enhancements help improve contrast, signal collection, and overall imaging performance.


****
2. **When should I choose Avant filters?**[Avant filters](https://www.idex-hs.com/news-events/stories-and-features/detail/maximize-fluorescence-performance) are best suited for fluorescence imaging applications that require the the narrowest separation between excitation and emission wavelengths. They are particularly valuable when working with short Stokes shift fluorophores such as mCherry, YFP, and Cy5.5, where maximizing signal collection while maintaining high contrast can be challenging. By enabling excitation and emission bands to be positioned closer together, Avant filters help capture more fluorescence signal without sacrificing signal to noise ratio.


****
3. **Are Essential Performance filters suitable for fluorescence imaging?** For fluorescence imaging,[BrightLine Basic filter sets](https://www.idex-hs.com/news-events/stories-and-features/detail/enhanced-fluorescence-imaging-brightline-filter-sets) provide cost-effective solutions that maintain Semrock quality while using relaxed specifications optimized for common fluorophores and imaging workflows.


4. **What are the best optical filter sets for flow cytometry applications?** The best optical filters for flow cytometry depend on detector architecture, fluorophore complexity, and instrument requirements. In spectral flow cytometry and other detector-based systems,[Nanopede filters](https://www.idex-hs.com/news-events/stories-and-features/detail/flow-cytometry-filters) provide evenly spaced spectral coverage across UV, visible, and near-infrared wavelengths, enabling flexible detector configurations and efficient channel separation.


****
5. **Which optical filters are recommended for Raman spectroscopy?** The[optimal Raman filter](https://www.idex-hs.com/resources/resources-detail/raman-catalog) depends on the spectral requirements of the application. EdgeBasic filters provide reliable performance for Raman systems with moderate requirements, while RazorEdge filters deliver deep laser-line blocking, narrow transition widths, and high transmission for demanding Raman measurements. For applications requiring detection closest to the laser line, Verona filters offer exceptionally narrow transition widths, low transmission ripple, and deep suppression of laser background. Pairing[MaxLine laser-line filters with RazorEdge filters](https://www.idex-hs.com/resources/resources-detail/razoredge-maxline-optical-filters-match) can further improve Raman signal collection and system performance.


****
6. **How do I choose the right optical filter for my application?** The right optical filter depends on your application, fluorophores, light source, detector, and performance requirements. For routine fluorescence imaging, cost-effective solutions such as BrightLine Basic may be sufficient. Advanced imaging systems using LEDs, lasers, or complex fluorophore panels may benefit from higher-performance options such as BrightLine, BrightLine 2.0 or Avant. For Raman spectroscopy, filter selection should also consider transition width, blocking performance, and proximity to the laser line. Evaluating the complete optical system helps ensure the filter is optimized for overall instrument performance. When in doubt,[tell us about your project](https://www.idex-hs.com/contact/contact-us/custom-optical-filters) . Our team of experts can help you select the exact filter for your application needs.


7. **When should fluorescence microscopy instrument manufacturers consider custom optical filters?**[Catalog filters](https://www.idex-hs.com/store/products/semrock_optical_filters/individual_optical_filters) provide short lead times and a broad range of specifications, which make them ideal for breadboarding and prototyping. Once your design is determined,[custom filters](https://www.idex-hs.com/capabilities/semrock-optical-filters/custom-optical-filters) let you tailor and refine the optics to your exact setup and achieve the maximum performance from your instrument. While catalog filters are suitable for many systems, custom optical filters can help maximize signal and/or signal-to-noise ratio; reduce instrument size and complexity; and create a more optimized optical path.


Manufacturers often transition from standard to custom filters as instruments move from prototype to production. By evaluating the full optical system, including fluorophores, detectors, light sources, and performance goals, custom filter designs can be engineered to improve imaging performance while supporting long-term manufacturing and supply chain requirements.
